text:
Maya: Heads up — ran the nightly billing recon and saw a cluster of credits appearing from replayed tokens that should have TTL-ed out. not sure if it's replay or late-arrival coupling. filing here before i escalate. :thinking_face:
Nisha: ah. which pipeline? accounting-ingest or postprocess?
Maya: looks like the postprocess consumer applies token TTL at enrichment time, but the replay path (backfill job) replays raw events into ingest which bypasses the TTL check. sample: tenant_id=acme, window=2026-03-15T02:00Z
Leo: ugh. so backfills are reintroducing tokens that were logically expired. that would inflate credits.
Sam: can we prove it's the TTL bypass? any trace ids?
Maya: i pulled this snippet from the recon log: `reconciler: credit_delta=+120.3, sample_event_id=evt_9f3b, seen_at=2026-03-16T04:12Z, original_ts=2026-03-01T01:02Z` — original_ts is outside charge window and should have been dropped earlier.
Jonah: timeline: 1) token emitted -> compact path marks TTL 30d 2) token expires at compact time 3) backfill job reads raw S3 blobs and republishes to ingest topic 4) ingest consumer rehydrates accounting events without TTL validation.
Nisha: Proposed quick playbook (short-term):
- stop backfill job (if running) :warning:
- add a temporary consumer-side filter that compares original_ts to allowed window and drops expired tokens (fast patch)
- run a bounded dry-run with `--dry-run` to see drop rate
Nisha: Example filter (pseudo):
```
if event.original_ts < now() - TOKEN_TTL:
    drop()
else:
    forward()
```
Leo: agree. medium term we need a canonical TTL-enforcement stage before any replayed messages enter accounting. That should live in the ingest gateway (common place).
Sam: ops question — will dropping in the consumer change downstream offsets in a way that confuses the reconciler?
Maya: no, drops still ack the message. we just don't emit a credit event. reconciler sees fewer credit events and that's expected.
Jonah: rollout plan suggestion:
1) patch consumer with filter behind feature flag (eng-platform feature flags)
2) enable for a small tenant slice (10%) for 6 hours, check reconciler diffs
3) expand to 100% after green
4) follow up with an ingest-gateway TTL enforcement RFC for a permanent fix
Sam: can we add quick metrics? `replay.expired_drops` counter + tag tenant_id to validate hotspots.
Maya: yes, i'll add the counter and a reconciler check query. sample prometheus: `sum(rate(replay_expired_drops[5m])) by (tenant_id)`
Nisha: backup plan if patch causes regressions: revert flag, re-run targeted reconcile to repair billing for affected tenants. ops runbook should include contact @oncall and finance-notify channel.
Leo: long-term design note: we should model expiry as a first-class attribute on events and have all ingestion pathways validate it (ingest-gateway, sidecar, and backfill tool). then backfills can include a `replay_metadata` header instead of bypassing validation.
Maya: i'll scope the RFC and include migration for historical events (best-effort reconciliation + doc for finance).
reconcile-bot: automated check: nightly-recon job detected 18 anomalous tenant deltas > $100 in last 24h, ticket #BILL-3421 created.
Sam: thanks. i can take the consumer patch and flagging. assigning to self. :thumbsup:
Maya: perfect. ping me on the rollout. i'll prep the prometheus dashboard and the reconciler diff query.
Nisha: leaving a short note for postmortem: include root cause (backfill bypass), decision (consumer filter -> ingest-gateway), and finance impact estimate.
Jonah: one more thing — please also capture how compact/TTL semantics interplay with compacter GC windows. those windows vary by tenant and could change enforcement logic.
Maya: added to RFC checklist. will update this thread with the patch PR link and dry-run numbers. :eyes:
